questions.q: The Bab-el-Mandeb Strait connects which two water bodies?
o: The Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman
The Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden
The Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea
The Black Sea and the Aegean Sea
questions.e: The strait lies between Yemen on the Arabian Peninsula and Djibouti and Eritrea in the Horn of Africa. Together with the Suez Canal, it forms the shipping route between the Mediterranean and the Indian Ocean.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong); PIB
questions.h: Gate of Tears: Red Sea to Gulf of Aden

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Strait of Hormuz:
1. It connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman.
2. Iran lies on its northern shore, while Oman and the United Arab Emirates lie to its south.
3. It connects the Red Sea with the Arabian Sea.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Hormuz is the only sea outlet of the Persian Gulf, so Gulf oil exports from Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kuwait and others pass through it. The Red Sea connects to the Arabian Sea through Bab-el-Mandeb and the Gulf of Aden.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Strait of Malacca:
1. It lies between the Malay Peninsula and the Indonesian island of Sumatra.
2. It connects the Andaman Sea with the South China Sea.
3. Singapore lies near its southern end.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The strait is the shortest sea route between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific, so it carries a large part of world trade. Singapore sits at its southern mouth, near the Singapore Strait.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of strait and the water bodies it connects:
1. Bosporus - Black Sea and Sea of Marmara
2. Dardanelles - Sea of Marmara and Aegean Sea
3. Kerch Strait - Black Sea and Sea of Azov
4. Strait of Messina - Sardinia and Corsica
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Bosporus and the Dardanelles together join the Black Sea to the Mediterranean through Turkey. The Strait of Messina separates mainland Italy from Sicily, while the Strait of Bonifacio separates Sardinia and Corsica.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Strait) with List-II (Landmasses it separates) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I: A. Bass Strait  B. Cook Strait  C. Torres Strait  D. Denmark Strait
List-II: 1. Mainland Australia and Tasmania  2. North Island and South Island of New Zealand  3. Australia and New Guinea  4. Greenland and Iceland
questions.e: Bass Strait lies south of Victoria state, Cook Strait divides New Zealand's two main islands, Torres Strait lies north of Cape York, and Denmark Strait lies between Greenland and Iceland.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Which one of the following water bodies lies between the southern tip of South America and Antarctica?
questions.e: Drake Passage links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans between Cape Horn and the Antarctic Peninsula. The Strait of Magellan runs between the South American mainland and Tierra del Fuego.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: The Bering Strait separates which two countries?
questions.e: It lies between Chukotka in Russia and Alaska in the United States, and joins the Pacific Bering Sea with the Arctic Chukchi Sea. The Diomede Islands lie within it.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)
questions.h: Two Diomedes: Russia and US a few km apart

questions.q: The Luzon Strait lies between which two places?
questions.e: It connects the South China Sea with the Philippine Sea. The Taiwan Strait separates China from Taiwan, the Korea Strait separates Korea from Japan, and the Tsugaru Strait separates Honshu from Hokkaido.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Madagascar is separated from the African mainland by which one of the following?
questions.e: The channel lies between Madagascar and Mozambique, and is a major shipping route around southern Africa. The Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea lie in the north-east and the Gulf of Guinea in the west.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: The Wallace Line, which marks a major biogeographical boundary, passes through which pair of straits?
questions.e: The line runs between Bali and Lombok and between Borneo and Sulawesi, separating the Asian and Australian fauna. Deep water there kept land bridges from forming even when sea levels fell.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong); NCERT

questions.q: Which one of the following countries does NOT have a coastline on the Caspian Sea?
questions.e: The Caspian is bordered by five countries: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan. Uzbekistan touches the Aral Sea basin but not the Caspian.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)
questions.h: Caspian five: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan

questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Romania
2. Georgia
3. Armenia
4. Hungary
How many of the above countries have a coastline on the Black Sea?
questions.e: The Black Sea is bordered by six countries: Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia. Armenia and Hungary are landlocked.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Which one of the following countries does NOT have a coastline on the Baltic Sea?
questions.e: Norway's coast lies on the North Sea, the Norwegian Sea and the Barents Sea. The Baltic is bordered by the Nordic, Baltic and Polish coasts and by Germany and Russia.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: The Dead Sea, the lowest land elevation on Earth, is bordered by which of the following?
o: Jordan, Israel and the West Bank
questions.e: It lies in the Jordan rift valley, over 400 metres below sea level, and its very high salinity prevents most life. The Jordan river flows into it from the north.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: The Sinai Peninsula lies between which two gulfs?
o: Gulf of Aden and Gulf of Oman
Gulf of Suez and Gulf of Aden
Gulf of Suez and Gulf of Aqaba
Gulf of Aqaba and Persian Gulf
questions.e: These two arms of the Red Sea flank the peninsula, which belongs to Egypt, and the Suez Canal forms its western boundary. The Gulf of Aqaba is where Jordan and Israel get their Red Sea outlets.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Which one of the following countries is landlocked?
questions.e: Ethiopia lost its coast when Eritrea became independent in 1993, and it now depends on ports such as Djibouti. Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan all touch the Red Sea or the Indian Ocean.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)
questions.h: Ethiopia lost its coast when Eritrea left in 1993

questions.q: Which one of the following countries does NOT share a land boundary with Afghanistan?
questions.e: Afghanistan borders Pakistan, Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and China. Kazakhstan lies north of Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan and does not touch it.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Which one of the following countries does NOT share a land boundary with China?
questions.e: China has 14 neighbours, including Laos, Kazakhstan and Bhutan. Thailand is separated from it by Myanmar and Laos.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Which one of the following countries does NOT share a land boundary with Iran?
questions.e: Iran borders Turkey, Iraq, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan. Kuwait lies south of Iraq on the Persian Gulf and has no land boundary with Iran.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Gaza Strip:
1. It lies on the Mediterranean coast.
2. It shares a land boundary with Egypt in the south.
3. It shares a land boundary with Jordan in the east.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Strip is a narrow coastal territory bordered by Israel in the north and east and by Egypt at Rafah in the south. The West Bank, not Gaza, borders Jordan.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong); PIB

questions.q: The Wakhan Corridor, a narrow strip of Afghan territory, extends up to the boundary of which country?
questions.e: It runs east between Tajikistan in the north and Pakistan in the south and ends at China's Xinjiang. It was kept as a buffer between the British and Russian empires.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave on the Baltic Sea, lies between which two countries?
questions.e: It is separated from the rest of Russia by those two European Union and NATO members, so Russia links to it by sea, air or through their territory. Its Baltic port is ice-free for most of the year.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Nile:
1. The Blue Nile rises from Lake Tana in Ethiopia.
2. The Blue Nile and the White Nile meet at Khartoum in Sudan.
3. The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam is built on the White Nile in Egypt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Blue Nile brings most of the water and silt, so Ethiopia's dam affects Sudan and Egypt downstream. The GERD is on the Blue Nile in Ethiopia, and the White Nile has its source in the Lake Victoria region.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong); PIB

questions.q: Which one of the following countries is NOT crossed by the Mekong river?
questions.e: The Mekong flows through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam before it reaches the South China Sea. Malaysia lies on the Malay Peninsula and the island of Borneo.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Tigris and Euphrates rivers:
1. Both rise in the highlands of Turkey.
2. Baghdad stands on the Tigris.
3. Their combined waters flow into the Persian Gulf as the Shatt al-Arab.
4. The Tigris flows through the Syrian capital Damascus.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The two rivers rise in eastern Turkey, cross Iraq and merge at Al-Qurna to form the Shatt al-Arab, which reaches the Gulf. Damascus lies on the Barada river and is not on the Tigris.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Which one of the following European capitals is NOT situated on the Danube?
questions.e: Prague stands on the Vltava, a tributary of the Elbe. The Danube flows through Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade before it reaches the Black Sea.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Which one of the following rivers flows into the Caspian Sea?
questions.e: The Volga, the longest river of Europe, ends in a delta on the Caspian near Astrakhan. The Don drains into the Sea of Azov, and the Dnieper and Danube into the Black Sea.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: The capital cities Kinshasa and Brazzaville face each other on opposite banks of which river?
questions.e: Kinshasa is the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Brazzaville of the Republic of the Congo. The Congo also crosses the equator twice.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)
questions.h: Congo river: two Congos, two capitals face to face

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Zambezi river:
1. Victoria Falls lies on it, on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe.
2. The Kariba Dam is built on it.
3. It flows into the Atlantic Ocean.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Zambezi flows east through Mozambique into the Indian Ocean after passing the Cahora Bassa dam. It does not reach the Atlantic, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Mountain peak) with List-II (Country) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I: A. Aconcagua  B. Kilimanjaro  C. Elbrus  D. Denali
List-II: 1. Argentina  2. Tanzania  3. Russia  4. United States
questions.e: Aconcagua in the Andes is the highest peak of the Americas, Kilimanjaro is Africa's highest, Elbrus in the Caucasus is Europe's highest by the usual boundary, and Denali in Alaska is the highest in North America.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of mountain range and the countries it lies in:
1. Pyrenees - France and Spain
2. Zagros - Iran and Iraq
3. Atlas - Egypt
4. Drakensberg - Argentina
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Pyrenees form the Franco-Spanish border, and the Zagros runs along the Iran-Iraq frontier. The Atlas is in north-west Africa (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia) and the Drakensberg in South Africa and Lesotho.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Desert) with List-II (Country) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I: A. Atacama  B. Namib  C. Taklamakan  D. Rub' al Khali
List-II: 1. Chile  2. Namibia  3. China  4. Saudi Arabia
questions.e: The Atacama lies on the Pacific coast of Chile, the Namib along Namibia's Atlantic coast, the Taklamakan in the Tarim basin of Xinjiang, and the Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter) in southern Saudi Arabia.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Desert) with List-II (Cold ocean current along its coast) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I: A. Atacama  B. Namib  C. Western Sahara  D. Western Australian desert
List-II: 1. Humboldt (Peruvian) current  2. Benguela current  3. Canary current  4. West Australian current
questions.e: Cold currents on the western coasts of continents cool the air above them, which stabilises it and prevents rain, so deserts reach the coast.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 14; Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)
questions.h: Cold current + trade winds = coastal desert

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Atacama desert is among the driest places on Earth.
Statement-II: It lies in the rain shadow of the Andes and is cooled by the cold Humboldt current.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: The Andes block moisture from the east, and the cold current offshore cools the air, making it stable so that clouds hardly form. The result is almost no rain in parts of the desert.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)
questions.h: Rain shadow + cold current = no rain

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Gobi is a cold desert.
Statement-II: It lies in the interior of Asia at a high elevation and in the rain shadow of high mountains.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Gobi on the Mongolia-China border is far from the sea, and the Tibetan plateau and the Himalaya block moisture-bearing winds. Its elevation and continental position make winters very cold.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of grassland and region:
1. Pampas - Argentina and Uruguay
2. Veldt - South Africa
3. Prairies - Eurasia
4. Downs - Canada
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Pampas of Argentina and Uruguay and the Veldt of South Africa are temperate grasslands. The Prairies are in North America, the Steppes in Eurasia and the Downs in Australia.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Which one of the following regions does NOT have a Mediterranean type of climate?
questions.e: The Mediterranean climate, with hot dry summers and mild wet winters, occurs on the western sides of continents between 30 and 40 degrees. Southern Brazil lies on the eastern side and has a humid sub-tropical climate.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 14

questions.q: Which one of the following countries is NOT crossed by the Equator?
questions.e: The Equator crosses Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil, Gabon, the Republic of the Congo, the DR Congo, Uganda, Kenya, Somalia and Indonesia, among others. Tanzania, with Mount Kilimanjaro, lies south of it.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 1

questions.q: Which one of the following countries is NOT crossed by the Prime Meridian (Greenwich)?
questions.e: The meridian passes through the United Kingdom, France, Spain, Algeria, Mali, Burkina Faso, Togo and Ghana. Nigeria lies east of it.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 1

questions.q: Which one of the following countries does NOT have a shoreline on Lake Victoria?
questions.e: Lake Victoria is shared by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania. Rwanda is in its wider basin but has no shoreline.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Which one of the following countries does NOT border Lake Chad?
questions.e: Lake Chad is shared by Chad, Cameroon, Niger and Nigeria. It has shrunk greatly because of drought and water withdrawals, which worsened livelihoods in the Sahel.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Lake Baikal, the world's deepest lake, is located in
questions.e: Baikal is a rift lake in southern Siberia holding about one-fifth of the world's surface fresh water. The Angara is its only outlet.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Which one of the following islands is shared by three countries?
questions.e: Borneo is divided among Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei. New Guinea, Hispaniola and Timor are each shared by two countries.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Suez Canal is one of the most important shipping routes of the world.
Statement-II: It lets ships travelling between Europe and Asia avoid the long route around the Cape of Good Hope.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The canal links the Mediterranean at Port Said with the Red Sea at Suez, and saves several thousand kilometres between Europe and the Indian Ocean. When the Red Sea route becomes unsafe, ships divert round southern Africa.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong); PIB

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Strait of Gibraltar:
1. It separates Spain from Morocco.
2. It connects the Atlantic Ocean with the Mediterranean Sea.
3. Ceuta, a Spanish city, lies on its southern shore in Africa.
4. It connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The strait is about 14 km wide at its narrowest and is the only natural entrance to the Mediterranean from the Atlantic. The Red Sea is joined to the Mediterranean by the Suez Canal.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: The Darien Gap, a region of dense rainforest and swamp that breaks the Pan-American Highway, lies between which two countries?
questions.e: It lies on the Panama-Colombia border, connecting Central and South America. It is a route used by many migrants moving north.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Territorial dispute) with List-II (Countries concerned) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I: A. Senkaku/Diaoyu Islands  B. Kuril Islands (Northern Territories)  C. Falkland Islands  D. Spratly Islands
List-II: 1. China and Japan  2. Russia and Japan  3. Argentina and the United Kingdom  4. China and several South-east Asian states
questions.e: The Senkaku/Diaoyu islets lie in the East China Sea, the Kurils between Hokkaido and Kamchatka, the Falklands in the South Atlantic and the Spratlys in the South China Sea, where Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei also have claims.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Transnistria, a breakaway region, is located along the Dniester river in which country?
questions.e: It is a strip between the Dniester and the Ukraine border that declared independence from Moldova in 1990 but is not recognised internationally. Abkhazia and South Ossetia are the comparable regions in Georgia.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: Which one of the following is the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.e: Sicily lies off the toe of the Italian peninsula, separated from it by the Strait of Messina. Sardinia, Cyprus and Crete are smaller.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)

questions.q: The Oresund (Sound) strait, linking the Baltic Sea with the Kattegat, separates which two countries?
questions.e: It lies between the Danish island of Zealand, where Copenhagen stands, and the Swedish province of Skane. A bridge-tunnel links Copenhagen with Malmo.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography (G C Leong)
